text.p: Trading company and retailer Ceteco Holding NV said on Monday it reiterated its previous forecast of an advance in sales and profits in 1996.

"The board of management stands by its earlier forecast that 1996 will see advances in sales and net income," the company, which is 70 percent owned by trading group Hagemeyer NV, said in a statement.
Ceteco posted 1995 net profit of 25.1 million guilders.
The company, which is mainly active in Latin America, said macroeconomic conditions in its markets could affect its full-year results.
"Given the growing sensitivity of group results to seasonal influences due to retailing operations' increasing share, the months of November and December will be of material importance," Ceteco said.

In the first half of 1996 net profits grew by 10.9 percent to 5.8 million guilders on 42.5 percent higher turnover of 287.4 million. Various acquisitions boosted first-half turnover but Ceteco said it had also seen sound organic growth.
The half-year figures reflected a difficult first quarter and a partly seasonal recovery in the second, it added.

Net financial charges increased to 23.4 million guilders from 13.9 million in the year-ago period. This was in line with the expansion of ongoing operations and the addition of new activities through acquisitions, Ceteco said.
